newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Nicaragua aims to double coffee yields in five yrs.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua aims to double coffee yields in five yrs.

text.p: Nicaragua, having seen coffee drop into second place as the country's foreign earnings product in 1996, is on a new drive to boost bean output, the executive secretary of the Nicaraguan Coffee Commission said Tuesday.

Alvaro Velazquez told Reuters at a meeting here of the Central American regional bloc of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) that the nation aims to boost production not through increasing the amount of coffee under cultivation but via better productivity.
"The idea is to boost productivity and double the yields of coffee per hectare," Velazquez said, adding the time frame was four to five years, building up gradually.

Velazquez said improved fertilzer use and management and more plant attention would be two focuses of the nation that this 1996-1997 cycle expects to see production of 950,000 quintales (100 lb or 46 kg bags) from the 1 million initially expected.
Velazquez said currently the country has an average yield per hectare of 12 quintales which he said should increase to 24- 25 quintales under optimum conditions and plant management.

But he said Nicaragua would not stray away from organic coffee farming to increase the yields. He said organic coffee farming plans would run in parallel to the increased yields drive that will be primarily promoted via seminars with growers.
Also, Velazquez said the country still planned to issue around $50 million in coffee bonds, given the problems of financing coffee farming in Nicaragua.

He said international finance groups, such as the International Monetary Fund, have put brakes on commercial banks loaning to coffee farmers because it is considered a high risk sector. Velazquez said this was one of the reasons why coffee revenues fell below those obtained from fishing last year.
